page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6986.33 and a PassMark CPU score of 8224.85. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1312.09 and lower single-threaded compression speeds. However, memory bandwidth remains solid, reaching 390.01 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and approximately 49.44 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database and caching performance are stable, with Redis SET operations achieving 6.6 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 6.27 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.c6.2xlarge is the lack of local storage and a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications or large local databases. However, its dedicated CPU allocation and AVX-512 instruction support make it a cost-efficient option for compute-bound workloads that do not require high memory footprints. It is well-suited for web serving, batch processing, and distributed microservices.
